**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 20 of the MSA meets the **preferred** position on every material term:

| Playbook element | Document |
|---|---|
| Vendor IP indemnity (services/deliverables) | ✅ 20.1, extends to Affiliates + personnel |
| Vendor breach of law / data breach / GN&WM | ✅ 20.2 (plus bodily injury & fraud) |
| Standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation) | ✅ 20.4, prejudice-limited, settlement consent |
| Remedy ladder (procure/modify/replace/refund) | ✅ 20.5, no termination of unaffected Services |
| Customer indemnity stays narrow | ✅ 20.3, Customer-supplied material + own breach of law, with Vendor-side carve-outs |

Two points that make this **better** than what we'd normally accept:

1. **No exclusions on the IP indemnity.** Clause 20.1 omits the customary Customer-modification / combination / specification carve-outs that even our fallback concedes. That's a Vendor-side gap in Vendor's favour to lose, not ours — so we leave it alone.
2. **Indemnity is uncapped.** Clause 21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims, so Section 20 sits outside the 21.1 cap altogether — stronger than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap.

One adjacent observation, flagged in the rationale rather than redlined here: the cap base in 21.1 is *"Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form"* — unusually narrow, since it ignores later Order Forms. That is a limitation-of-liability problem and belongs to that rule; it does not touch this indemnity, which is carved out of the cap. Raising it under INDEMN would double-flag the same commercial term.
